blocks.raw: <WikiExamTable rows={[{"heading":"Challenge / Concept","description":"Philippine Application and Constraint"},{"content":"Metro Manila as Primate City","description":"Manila's population (~14M in metro area) is ~7× larger than Cebu (~2M). Violates rank-size rule. Causes congestion, slum growth, infrastructure strain. National policy seeks to develop satellite growth centers (Laguna, Pampanga, Davao) to decentralize."},{"content":"Concentric Zone Model in PH Context","description":"Model applies to formal urban core but breaks down in sprawl areas where informal settlement, landgrabbing, and leapfrog development dominate. Informal land occupation defies model's assumptions about property markets."},{"content":"CLUP Implementation Gaps","description":"RA 7160 mandates CLUP; DHSUD reviews for conformity. But many LGUs lack technical staff to monitor zoning compliance. Sanggunian may be politically influenced to rezone agricultural land to residential without infrastructure planning. Implementation gap between CLUP vision and actual development."},{"content":"Informal Settlements and In-Situ Upgrading","description":"RA 7279 requires relocation for danger areas but permits in-situ upgrading where possible. CMP (Community Mortgage Program) enables communities to stay in place. Philippine strategy: upgrade informality in place rather than mass relocation (more cost-effective, socially preferred)."},{"content":"Balanced Housing in Market Projects","description":"RA 7279 and RA 10884 require developers to produce socialized housing. Specific percentage requirements vary by LGU ordinance and project classification; verify current DHSUD guidelines for applicable raRA 7279 (Housing and Urban Development Coordinating Council Act) and RA 10884 (Balanced Housing Development Act of 2016) require developers to produce socialized housing. RA 10884 refined and expanded balanced housing requirements beyond RA 7279. BGC, Makati, Las Piñas developments include socialized towers alongside market towers. Implementation: on-site, off-site, or NHA partnership options.ns."},{"content":"Transit-Oriented Development (TOD)","description":"MRT/LRT stations are natural nodes. TOD zoning allows higher density around stations (400–800m catchment). BGC and Makati CBD applied TOD; provincial cities lag. Challenge: informal transport (tricycles, jeepneys) not fully integrated with formal transit."},{"content":"New Urbanism in BGC and Planned Developments","description":"BGC, Laguna's Technopark, Cavite growth centers apply NU principles (mixed use, walkability, street-facing shops, 400m blocks). But retrofitting existing sprawl to NU density is harder than greenfield development. Real estate economics favor density, but infrastructure must follow."},{"content":"Felino Palafox Jr. Influence","description":"Leading PH urban planner. Masterplanned BGC, regional growth centers, numerous LGU CLUPs. Represents bridge between international NU/TOD theory and Philippine realities (informal settlements, limited capacity, rapid growth)."}]} />

blocks.raw: <Tip>Philippine planning = applying international theory to local reality (informal settlements, weak capacity, rapid sprawl, diverse stakeholders). Felino Palafox Jr. = leading contemporary planner. In-situ upgrading = keep communities in place. CLUP = law-mandated; zoning ordinance = implementation tool; DHSUD = reviews for conformity.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Treating the Concentric Zone Model as literally describing Manila's geography — it describes formal urban expansion; informal settlement and leapfrog development violate the model's assumptions","Confusing CLUP (a vision document) with zoning ordinance (the legal implementation) — both are necessary; one without the other fails","Thinking RA 7279 relocation is always used — actually, in-situ upgrading is preferred when possible (CMP), and relocation is used mainly for danger areas","Underestimating Felino Palafox Jr.'s role in contemporary Philippine planning — he is not just a name to know; his work in BGC and LGU CLUPs is foundational to modern PH urbanism","Assuming all LGUs have equal planning capacity — reality: large cities (QC, Makati, Cebu) have professional planners; many municipalities lack capacity and depend on consultants"]} />
